newsitem.title: GHANA: Two consortia join search for Ghana's oil and gas.
newsitem.headline: Two consortia join search for Ghana's oil and gas.

text.p: Ghana has signed oil and gas exploration and production agreements with two foreign consortiums, one U.S.-South Korean and one British, the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) said on Monday.
It said the agreements, covering areas off the western part of Ghana's coast, were signed last Friday by Finance Minister Kwame Peprah and executives of GNPC and the foreign oil companies.
Nuevo Ghana Inc., a subsidiary of Nuevo Energy Co of the U.S. and Yukong Ltd of South Korea, will operate in the eastern Cape Three Points Sub-Basin.

Seafield Resources of the U.K. and Dana Ghana Ltd, a subsidiary of London-based Dana Exploration Plc Petroleum Inc. which GNPC officials said was incorporated in Ireland, will operate in the western Cape Three Points Sub-Basin.
The Cape Three Points Sub-Basin is part of the Tano Basin on the border with Ivory Coast.
The two consortiums are to spend about $6 million each on the projects, GNPC said.
GNPC will not invest directly but will be a collaborator and obtained a 10 percent carried interest which can be increased to 20 percent upon commercial discovery.

Last month Hunt Overseas Exploration Company (Ghana) L.P., an affiliate of Hunt Oil Cy of Dallas, Texas, signed an agreement granting Hunt a 10,000 sq km deepwater exploration concession in the same area.

In March 1996, Hunt obtained a 4,300 sq km concession in the area and has so far invested $3 million. Hunt's preliminary exploration results are very encouraging, GNPC's chief executive told reporters last month.
Natural gas was discovered in the Cape Three Points Sub-Basin as far back as 1974 by Phillips Petroleum. The discovery well flowed at 3.9 million cubic feet per day.

Interest in the reserves believed to be 287 billion cubic feet rose sharply when GNPC's ambitious floating power plant project took off in April 1996. The U.S. Export-Import Bank approved financing of $316 million for the project in which natural gas will be used to fire the 148 megawatt power plant.
Mounted on two barges to be moored in a lagoon, the plant is to start electricity generation by the end of next year. The first barge is being built by Westinghouse of Orlando, Florida.

Interest in Ghana's natural gas reserves is also on the increase because of the West Africa Pipeline project, a planned offshore natural gas pipeline to link Nigeria, Benin, Togo, Ghana and eventually Ivory Coast.
